statements.claim: Yashoda chased Krishna with a stick to punish him for the broken butter pot, but dropped it when she saw his fear.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.11 (tyaktvā yaṣṭiṃ sutaṃ bhītaṃ vijñāyārbhaka-vatsalā); broken pot from prior story DKS_0033 per corpus chain

statements.claim: Every rope she tied came up short by two fingers' width.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.14-15; pack excerpt: 'always two fingers too short to bind him'

statements.claim: She joined rope after rope from her own house and still the gap would not close.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.16 (evaṃ sva-geha-dāmāni yaśodā sandadhaty api)

statements.claim: She sweated; her braid and garland came loose as she worked.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.17 (svinna-gātrāyā visrasta-kabara-srajaḥ)

statements.claim: Krishna, whom no being in the worlds could bind, of his own accord let the rope close around him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.18-20 (bhṛtya-vaśyatā; neither Virincha/Brahma, Bhava/Shiva nor Shri can grasp him); pack excerpt

statements.claim: Yashoda bound him to the great wooden mortar.
statements.evidence: Pack canonical event evt_0048; VP 5.6 passage (in DKS_0038 pack): 'Fastening a cord round his waist, she tied him to the wooden mortar'

notes: All claims grounded in BP 10.9.11-20 and the pack's rendered excerpt; no unsupported or contradicted statements.

statements.claim: The cowherds heard the crash of the falling trees and came running to find the child by the uprooted arjuna trees.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.27ff; pack excerpt: 'the cowherds hear the crash and marvel'

statements.claim: Two radiant figures rose from the fallen trees, shining like fire just kindled.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.27 (śriyā paramayā ... kujayor iva jāta-vedāḥ)

statements.claim: They were Nalakuvara and Manigriva, and the curse that held them was over.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.41 (nalakūvara); pack summary

statements.claim: They bowed with joined palms and praised Krishna as the great yogi, the first and highest person, Lord of all beings, subtle source, Vasudeva.
They asked that their voices, ears, hands, minds, heads and eyes be forever turned to him and his devotees.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.37 (vāṇī ... śravaṇau ... hastau ... manas ... śiras ... dṛṣṭiḥ)

statements.claim: Krishna told them they were his, with hearts fixed on him, and bade them go to their own home.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.40-41 (sādhūnāṃ sama-cittānāṃ ... tad gacchataṃ mat-paramau nalakūvara sādanam)

statements.claim: They departed toward the north, free at last.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'released from their curse, depart to the north'

statements.claim: The cowherds could not explain what they saw and sensed the child was not simply a child.
statements.evidence: Consistent with pack excerpt ('the cowherds hear the crash and marvel'); the fear/recognition is narrative inference

notes: All praises, requests, and the dismissal map to BP 10.10.27-43. The northward departure is supported by the pack's own index summary.

statements.claim: Krishna danced whenever the cowherd women clapped and coaxed him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.6 (gopībhiḥ stobhito 'nṛtyad bhagavān bālavat)

statements.claim: When his father asked, he fetched the stool, weights, and wooden sandals.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.7 (pīṭhakonmāna-pādukam)

statements.claim: Hearing the fruit-seller's cry to buy fruits, Krishna hurried out with a fistful of grain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.9 (krīṇīhi bhoḥ phalānīti śrutvā satvaram acyutaḥ)

statements.claim: The grain spilled from his hands before he reached the seller, leaving his fists nearly empty.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.10 (phala-vikrayiṇī tasya cyuta-dhānya-kara-dvayam)

statements.claim: She filled his small hands with fruit and found her basket filled with jewels where the fruit had been.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'the fruit-seller finds her basket filled with jewels where her fruit had been'; index summary

statements.claim: Grain was what a village that kept no coins gave and took.
statements.evidence: Setting context; not a sourceable claim in the pack

statements.claim: She had given to the one who gives everything back a hundredfold.
statements.evidence: Devotional framing consistent with the episode's import

notes: All episode facts grounded in BP 10.11.6-10.

statements.claim: Upananda, a cowherd superior in wisdom and age, called the cowherds together and urged leaving Gokula for its welfare.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.21-22 (upānanda ... gopo jñāna-vayo-'dhikaḥ; utthātavyam ito 'smābhir gokulasya hitaiṣibhiḥ)

statements.claim: He cited the demoness who came to kill children, from whom the boy was saved.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.23 (muktaḥ kathañcid rākṣasyā bāla-ghnyā)

statements.claim: A whirlwind demon carried him into the sky, yet he came down alive.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.24 (cakra-vātena nīto 'yaṃ daityena vipadaṃ viyat)

statements.claim: He passed between the two great trees and did not die.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.25 (yan na mriyeta drumayor antaraṃ prāpya bālakaḥ)

statements.claim: As an infant he overturned the waggon with a kick of his foot, its pots and pans flung across the ground.
statements.evidence: VP 5.6 (Wilson): 'kicking up his feet he overturned the vehicle, and all the pots and pans were upset and broken'

statements.claim: Vrindavana was fresh, new pastureland good for the cattle, a place where the omens of Gokula would have no hold.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.27 (vanaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ nāma paśavyaṃ nava-kānanam); VP 5.6: 'where terrestrial prodigies may no more disturb us'

statements.claim: He urged them to yoke the carts and go at once, without delay.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.28 (tat tatrādyaiva yāsyāmaḥ śakaṭān yuṅkta mā ciram)

statements.claim: The cowherds agreed, saying 'well said,' and the colony moved with its elders, children, women, and belongings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.11.29-30 (sādhu sādhv iti vādinaḥ; vṛddhān bālān striyo rājan sarvopakaraṇāni ca)

statements.claim: Groves that had never been grazed, grass that had not been cropped.
statements.evidence: Elaboration of 'nava-kānanam' (new grove); no contradictory claim in pack

notes: Omens list matches BP 10.11.23-25 plus the waggon from VP 5.6, exactly as the pack assembles them.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama (Samkarshana) passed seven years in Vraja.
statements.evidence: HV 1.58.1: 'passed their childhood in Vraja and became seven years old'

statements.claim: They wore dark-blue and yellow garments, yellow and white paste, and crow feathers while tending cattle.
Their forest play: leaf crowns and wild-flower garlands like young trees, lotus crowns, a rope as sacred thread, gourds, flutes, leaf beds, running like young horses, beautifying the forest.
The forest was ruined: grass and twigs gone, trees uprooted by the milkmen, cow-shed fires scorching trunks, birds fled, no sweet winds, like rice without curry.
Where droppings fell on the grass, the grazing soured and the milk turned poor.
Vrindavana lay on the Yamuna's bank with thick grass, no thorns or insects, fruit and kadamba trees, and cool winds like an asylum of all seasons.
Govardhana rose high like Mandara; the Bhandira fig tree spread a yojana like a dark cloud; the Kalindi (Yamuna) ran through the middle like a parting in hair.
Krishna decided to create a calamity to frighten the milkmen into leaving.
statements.evidence: HV 1.58.29 ('Let us now, creating some calamity, terrify the milk-men')

statements.claim: From the hairs of his body arose hundreds of wolves living on fat, blood and flesh, dark-faced, bearing the Srivatsa mark, in groups of five, ten, twenty, thirty and a hundred.
statements.evidence: HV 1.58.30ff: 'From the hairs of his body there arose hundreds of wolves living on fat, blood and flesh ... groups of five, ten, thirty, twenty and a hundred those dark-faced wolves, bearing the mystic mark of Srivatsa'

statements.claim: The wolves fell upon the calves, cows and women, striking terror into the milkmen.
statements.evidence: HV 1.58: 'Beholding them fall upon calves, kine and their women the milk-men were stricken with great fear'

statements.claim: Krishna did not mean to harm his own people; he meant to move them.
statements.evidence: Interpretive framing consistent with HV's 'terrify the milk-men' intent

notes: Every description (garments, forest ruin, Vrindavana geography, wolves) matches HV 1.58 nearly verbatim.

statements.claim: Uddhava recalled Krishna herding calves, surrounded by them, sporting in the Yamuna's groves.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.26 (parīto vatsapair vatsāṃś cārayan vyaharad vibhuḥ)

statements.claim: He showed the cowherds his childhood play, lovely to watch.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.27 (kaumārīṃ darśayaṃś ceṣṭāṃ prekṣaṇīyāṃ vrajaukasām)

statements.claim: He was a child who wept and laughed in the same hour, with the bright boldness of a lion cub.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'weeping and laughing with a lion-cub's glance' (BP 3.2.26-29 rendering)

statements.claim: His flute playing delighted the cowherds.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'playing the flute, he delighted the cowherds'

statements.claim: Kamsa, the Bhoja king, never stopped sending shape-shifting demon agents against him.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.29 (prayuktān bhoja-rājena māyinaḥ kāma-rūpiṇaḥ)

statements.claim: Kamsa was Krishna's own cruel uncle.
statements.evidence: 'Bhoja king' supported by BP 3.2.29; uncle relation is corpus-established context (DKS_0333: Devaki calls Kamsa 'that eldest brother of mine'), cruelty shown by the demons he sent

statements.claim: Krishna dispelled the demons in sport, as easily as a child knocks aside toys.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'he dispelled in sport, like toys'

notes: Recollection matches BP 3.2.26-29 exactly; no unsupported or contradicted event claims.

statements.claim: While his mother was busy with household duties, Krishna caught sight of the two arjuna trees.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.21 (kṛṣṇas tu gṛha-kṛtyeṣu vyagrāyāṃ mātari prabhuḥ)

statements.claim: The trees were formerly Nalakuvara and Manigriva, sons of Kubera, turned into trees by Narada's curse because of pride.
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.22 (purā nārada-śāpena vṛkṣatāṃ prāpitau madāt); pack excerpt

statements.claim: They had moved among the guhyakas, the celestial attendants of their father's realm.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'the guhyaka sons of Kubera'

statements.claim: The two trees stood side by side, tall and straight, branches lacing overhead.
statements.evidence: Descriptive scene-setting; not a pack claim

statements.claim: No one in the village knew the trees' secret, and the child was the one who could undo the curse.
statements.evidence: Foreshadowing framing consistent with the arc (DKS_0035/0036 uprooting)

notes: Facts match BP 10.9.21-22; the rest is scene-setting consistent with the surrounding episodes.

statements.claim: Nalakuvara and Manigriva, sons of Kubera the lord of wealth, drank varuni wine and, eyes rolling with intoxication, sported naked in the Ganga among lotus groves with celestial women.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.2-3 (vāruṇīṃ madirāṃ pītvā madāghūrṇita-locanau; antaḥ praviśya gaṅgāyām ambhoja-vana-rājini)

statements.claim: Kubera's home was on Mount Kailasa.
statements.evidence: Pack index entry locations: 'Kailasa, Ganga river'

statements.claim: Narada happened by; the naked women, fearing a curse, covered themselves, but the pride-blinded brothers did not.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.4-6 (taṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍitā devyo vivastrāḥ śāpa-śaṅkitāḥ; tau dṛṣṭvā madirā-mattau śrī-madāndhau surātmajau)

statements.claim: Narada taught that the body, though called divine, ends as worms, filth and ashes, comes from father and mother, and returns to the unmanifest; that poverty is the best medicine for pride; that the poor are free of ego; and that sages of equal vision draw near the poor, in whose company one learns to want only Mukunda's feet.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.8-17 (kṛmi-viḍ-bhasma-saṃjñitam; sādhāraṇaṃ deham avyakta-prabhavāpyayam; dāridryaṃ param añjanam; daridro nirahaṃ-stambho; daridrasyaiva yujyante sādhavaḥ sama-darśinaḥ; mukunda-caraṇaiṣiṇām)

statements.claim: He cursed them: sons of the world's protector sunk in darkness, they would stand as trees, rooted and motionless.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.18-20 (loka-pālasya putrau bhūtvā tamaḥ-plutau; ato 'rhataḥ sthāvaratāṃ syātāṃ)

statements.claim: After a hundred years of the gods they would come into the presence of Vasudeva and be set free.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.21 (vāsudevasya sānnidhyaṃ labdhvā divya-śarac-chate); pack excerpt 'promising release at the touch of Vasudeva'

statements.claim: So they became twin arjuna trees, the curse also serving as their cure.
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.22ff and DKS_0041 pack (vṛkṣatāṃ prāpitau); the 'cure' reading is consistent with the promised release

notes: All elements of the curse episode map to BP 10.10.1-22; the Kailasa setting is in the pack's own index locations.
